## Scope

One-time read-only integrity review under #516, independent of M7 product implementation. Start with the selected save tree: game saves, save states, screenshots and their metadata. Do not recursively download a ROM/content library or expand to large archives without a stated scope. Exact provider identities, account paths, filenames, hashes, file bytes and findings remain in a restricted local record; this issue retains redacted outcomes only.

Compare cloud bytes against provider-supplied content hashes and any independently available local counterparts. A matching current hash proves readable/consistent bytes, not the historically correct game progress or successful loading in every core. Validate recognizable containers/images and report unsupported/raw formats honestly. Retain prior log/timeline observations as separate evidence. Source inspection and local readback determine which migration settings/records changed; do not replace local saves or edit pointers based on a cloud rewind alone.

## Maintainer requirements

> All that really matters is that we're able to verify the contents of the folder to ensure it's not corrupted, which is something we'll want to be doing anyway. We can also look at this as a chance to ensure that our verification process is working correctly. This doesn't replace any of the entries you might be doing to double-check. I do want to make sure my saves are still in a good spot. I likely need to create a second level of redundancy for how they're saved, but that's a separate project we'll tackle later.

> Also, while I made all the changes on the cloud, I realized I haven't even asked if we made any changes on the device and if we need to redo any of the files on the device.

> Also, if there are any general items we learned from this exercise that would help us in any of our future issues we've outlined to accomplish, we should take this as a learning opportunity as well. Sort of a hand-picked manual verification process we can incorporate into our automated verification, potentially if relevant

## Work and acceptance criteria

- [x] A scoped inventory binds current cloud size/hash/identity before and after reads; bounds, unsupported hashes, changed files, download failures and exclusions cannot be reported as passes. Raw records remain private.
- [x] Downloaded save-tree bytes match provider hashes; compare local counterparts read-only and distinguish equal, differing, absent and unreadable. No direction/winner is inferred from timestamps alone.
- [x] Recognized file types receive structural checks with explicit limits. Raw/core-specific saves without a parser remain unverified for game semantics; per-file outcomes separate byte integrity, structural integrity and playability.
- [x] Disposable synthetic controls prove the verifier accepts valid data and rejects changed/truncated/missing files, incorrect hashes and invalid supported containers. No corruption is injected into personal originals.
- [x] Exact installed-source tracing lists local config/recovery state written by the migration and any local payload effects. A concrete proposed alignment names files/keys and old/new behavior; no device mutation, reboot or sync occurs without separately named approval.
- [x] A redacted report and private per-file evidence explain findings and remaining limits, retaining the earlier log checks. Large-library verification remains outside this small-save scope and requires separate explicit planning; independent backup redundancy is tracked in #518; no product validator readiness result is mislabeled a full-content check.

Can this be done on the VM? Verifier failure controls use isolated synthetic host files (and VM only if target-runtime behavior is involved). Actual private saved bytes and existing local state require read-only operational observation; they are not release QA fixtures. Use the existing authorized read route, no secret export, no uploads/deletes/moves. Any long run uses watch-job with active result delivery and compact retained receipts. Retire downloaded scratch after its named checks; retain protected evidence, not an accidental new backup project.

## Reusable outcome (D-CLOUD-181)

- [x] Useful manual findings become host synthetic controls and a documented protocol; #515/#508 explicitly carry the relevant repair/adoption cases without personal fixtures or expanding setup into full-library verification.

`tools/cloud-save-integrity`, `tools/cloud-save-integrity-test` and `docs/cloud-save-integrity.md` provide scoped offline checks and 24 passing synthetic controls. The private operational inventory/read/local-comparison receipts and installed-source alignment proposal are complete; precise findings remain restricted locally. The observed checks found no need to replace game-save payloads. No device/cloud mutation occurred. This does not certify historical progress or core compatibility. Cleanup/alignment remains separately owned by #516, and redundancy is deferred under #518. Published on `next` as `1bd4554dc8e90a3211787c5986ca581aeaaa82a6`. Evidence: `docs/qa-logs/2026-10-08-save-integrity/`; protocol: `docs/cloud-save-integrity.md`. Required gates passed; the separately owed M7 audit remains #507.
